metadata.rules_text:
- When sentiment is consistently negative over recent days, model tends to underpredict (forecast too low) — adjust upward by 1–2% of recent mean or median.
- After a sharp price spike (e.g., >5% from prior peak), model often overreacts and overshoots — cap forecast at 10–15% above recent peak or use moving average to smooth.
- If true outcome shows strong mean reversion (e.g., 3–5 consecutive days below 38–40), model tends to lag — add 1–2 days of “reversion buffer” in forecast, or shift mean to recent 7-day average.
- When sentiment flips from negative to positive (or vice versa), model often misreads momentum — delay forecast adjustment by 1–2 days or use sentiment-weighted smoothing (e.g., 70% recent, 30% sentiment).
- For 30-day horizon, model frequently underestimates late-period volatility — add 0.5–1.5% buffer to final 5–7 days if sentiment is volatile or event-driven.
- If true outcome shows “late surge” (e.g., last 3–5 days > 40), model often misses it — forecast last 5 days with 1–2% higher slope or use exponential decay weighting on recent data.
